_meta.description: Mishaps (ruling 142): things that happen to the ship on a travel leg that nobody chose. The cruise screen stops on a popup the player must acknowledge, and the Ship's Log records it in red. Rolled once per leg (never the leg into the destination) by engine/js/mishaps.js. A mishap's tier is minor, moderate or severe; a tier's `fixed` version plays instead when its role is aboard and comes through (a crew specialist always, a captain of that background or a wounded specialist half the time). Low hull makes hull mishaps likelier and worse (ruling 143).
_meta.tier_fields: text (narrator, deadpan, no '!'), resources {fuel,food,water,o2,hull,gold} (costs scale by odds.cost_mult per trail), crop_health, hurt {who: captain|crew|anyone, hp: n} or {who, severity: injury|delayed|lethal}, fixed {role, text, resources?, crop_health?, hurt?}
_meta.tokens: {crew.<role>} (whoever holds the role; 'the captain' when the captain does), {who} / {Who} (the one hurt)

minor.text: A thin whistle from the aft corridor. A grain of something has put a hole in the hull roughly the size of a regret. Someone covers it with chewing gum. It holds.

moderate.text: The hole is the size of a coin and does not respond to gum. The air finds it before anyone else does.

fixed.text: {crew.engineer} has a patch on it before the alarm finishes its first sentence.

severe.text: Something small and fast goes through two bulkheads and out the other side. The ship vents for eleven seconds, which is a long time to listen to air leave.

fixed.text: Something small and fast goes through two bulkheads. {crew.engineer} seals the inner hole by leaning on it until the foam sets. The outer one is left to the auto-patch, which tries.

minor.text: A seam in the cargo bay creaks in a new key. On inspection it is a hairline crack. It is noted, photographed and left to think about what it has done.

moderate.text: A weld seam along the port spine gives up a few centimetres of its commitment. The hull readout drops and stays dropped.

fixed.text: A weld seam starts to open. {crew.engineer} rewelds it in the time it takes everyone else to find the manual.

severe.text: The spine seam opens along a metre of its length with a sound like a door the size of a ship. Frost forms on the inside of the cargo bay. Then it stops, mostly.

fixed.text: The spine seam opens along a metre of its length. {crew.engineer} bolts a strongback across it and declares it structural, which is a lie the ship believes.

minor.text: The cargo hatch seal sighs. Someone kicks it. It stops sighing.

moderate.text: The cargo hatch seal fails quietly overnight. By morning the hold is cold and the oxygen reading has a lower opinion of the ship.

severe.text: The forward hatch seal blows out with a bang that knocks the coffee off every surface aboard. The emergency door drops in time. Most of the air stays on the right side of it.

minor.text: Something pings off the bow. The sensors call it debris. The debris does not comment.

moderate.text: A tumbling chunk of somebody's old satellite catches the hull broadside. Paint, plating and a commemorative plaque are lost.

severe.text: Debris hits hard enough to throw everyone sideways. {Who} goes into a bulkhead shoulder first. The hull takes it worse.

minor.text: A hull plate starts to rattle at cruising speed. It sounds like a polite knock. It is ignored, like most polite things.

moderate.text: A rattling hull plate shakes itself free and leaves. The ship is a little lighter and a little less armoured.

severe.text: Three plates go in a row, peeling off like scales. What was under them was not designed to be looked at.

fixed.text: Plates start peeling off the hull in a row. {crew.engineer} goes out on a tether and staples the rest down with the riveter and a great deal of language.

minor.text: Someone carrying a fuel sample trips in the corridor. Most of it ends up on the floor and some of it ends up on the ceiling, which nobody can explain.

moderate.text: A transfer canister tips over in the engine room and empties itself into the deck drain with the efficiency of a thing that has wanted this for a long time.

severe.text: A full transfer canister ruptures on its way to the tank. The engine room smells of it for days. The tank does not.

minor.text: A drip under the main fuel line. A rag is wedged under it. The rag is now the most valuable fabric aboard.

moderate.text: The main fuel line weeps at a coupling for most of the leg before anyone thinks to check why the gauge is shy.

fixed.text: The main fuel line starts weeping at a coupling. {crew.engineer} smells it, finds it and torques it shut before it costs much.

severe.text: A fuel line splits clean through. The feed shuts itself off, eventually. The word 'eventually' is doing a great deal of work.

fixed.text: A fuel line splits clean through. {crew.engineer} clamps it with both hands and a belt until the bypass comes on.

minor.text: A vent valve sticks open for a few seconds and then remembers itself.

moderate.text: A vent valve sticks open and stays there, venting fuel into space at a steady, unbothered rate.

fixed.text: A vent valve sticks open. {crew.pilot} sees the burn go lopsided, cuts the feed by hand and trims the ship around the loss.

severe.text: The vent valve jams wide open mid-burn. The ship spins a quarter turn on the escaping fuel before the cutoff trips, and something structural complains about it.

fixed.text: The vent valve jams wide open mid-burn. {crew.pilot} catches the spin on the thrusters and kills the feed by hand. The ship never quite turns.

minor.text: The last refill was cut with something. The engine notices. It burns a little extra to make its point.

moderate.text: The last refill was mostly fuel and partly a decision someone else made. The engine burns through it like it is angry.

severe.text: The last refill was barely fuel at all. The engine coughs, burns twice what it should, and fouls an injector doing it.

minor.text: The CO2 scrubber wheezes. Someone pulls a sock out of it. Nobody claims the sock.

moderate.text: The CO2 scrubber clogs overnight. Everyone wakes up with a headache and the same bad idea at once.

fixed.text: The CO2 scrubber clogs. {crew.engineer} has it apart and back together before the headaches set in.

severe.text: The scrubber's bed cracks and dumps its whole load back into the air. The ship spends two days on the reserve and everyone talks slowly.

fixed.text: The scrubber's bed cracks. {crew.engineer} rigs a spare from the growbay's filter stack and the reserve only takes half the hit.

minor.text: An oxygen tank valve ticks open and shut on its own. It is told to stop. It stops.

moderate.text: An oxygen tank bleeds through a bad valve into the vacuum side of the bulkhead for most of a day.

severe.text: An oxygen tank's valve shears off. The tank empties in under a minute. The other tanks watch.

minor.text: Toast, but in the sense of a small fire. It is put out with a lid.

moderate.text: A grease fire in the galley. The suppressant works, the extractor works, and lunch does not survive.

fixed.text: A grease fire in the galley. {crew.chef} smothers it with a pan without putting down the other pan.

severe.text: The galley catches properly. By the time the suppressant wins, the stores behind it are smoke and {who} has burns up one arm.

minor.text: You slip on a wet patch of corridor and land with dignity, or near it.

moderate.text: You slip on a wet patch of corridor and land on the edge of a step. It hurts in a way that has opinions.

severe.text: You go down a ladder faster than the ladder intended. Something cracks, and it is not the ladder.

minor.text: You put a hand on a coolant return that is not, it turns out, returning anything cool.

moderate.text: A steam line lets go beside you in the engine room. You get out with most of your skin.

severe.text: A steam line lets go in your face. The burns are bad, and by the next day they are not healing the way burns should.

minor.text: A locker door you did not latch swings out on a turn and introduces itself to your elbow.

moderate.text: A locker you did not latch empties itself across the corridor at you during a burn. You stop most of it with your ribs.

severe.text: An unsecured equipment rack comes off its rail in a hard burn with you between it and the wall.

minor.text: {Who} grabs a junction box that was supposed to be dead. It was not. Hair, briefly, is interesting.

moderate.text: {Who} takes a proper jolt off a frayed conduit and spends the afternoon not feeling one hand.

severe.text: {Who} is thrown clear of a shorting panel and does not get up for a long, quiet minute.

minor.text: Lunch was off. Everybody knew. Everybody ate it anyway. A day of regret follows.

moderate.text: A batch of rations had turned. {Who} ate the most of it, by a margin nobody wants to discuss.

fixed.text: {crew.chef} sniffs the stew, says one word, and puts the whole pot out the airlock. Nobody gets sick.

severe.text: Half the cold store had spoiled without the alarm saying so. {Who} is properly sick for days.

fixed.text: Half the cold store had spoiled without the alarm saying so. {crew.chef} catches it before anyone eats from it, and saves what can be saved.

minor.text: A water tank weeps at a fitting. It is tightened. Everyone feels a little thirstier anyway.

moderate.text: A water tank cracks along a seam and empties a good part of itself into the bilge, where it cannot be drunk without a great deal of courage.

fixed.text: A water tank cracks along a seam. {crew.engineer} pumps it across to the spare before the bilge gets much.

severe.text: A water tank splits wide. By the time anyone gets there it is a puddle with ambitions.

fixed.text: A water tank splits wide. {crew.engineer} saves half of it with a pump, a hose and a lot of running.

minor.text: A crate of rations turns out to be a crate of opinions about rations. It goes out the airlock.

moderate.text: The cold store's seal failed sometime last week. A shelf of food is now a shelf of chemistry.

fixed.text: The cold store's seal failed. {crew.chef} salvages most of it into a soup nobody asks about.

severe.text: The cold store's compressor died days ago and told no one. Most of what was in there is gone.

fixed.text: The cold store's compressor died days ago. {crew.chef} cooks, dries and pickles what can be saved in one long night.

minor.text: The lights flicker. The ship carries on as if it had not noticed, which is how ships deal with feelings.

moderate.text: A power surge trips the growbay lamps for most of a day. The crop spends it in the dark, wondering.

severe.text: A surge cooks a bus bar. The growbay goes dark and cold for two days and a junction in the wall melts into modern art.

minor.text: The growbay pump stalls and restarts. The crop does not seem to mind. It may not have noticed.

moderate.text: The growbay pump stalls overnight. By morning the soil is dry and the crop looks betrayed.

fixed.text: The growbay pump stalls. {crew.botanist} hears the silence where the trickle should be and hand-waters until it is fixed.

severe.text: The growbay pump seizes and floods one bed while starving the rest.

fixed.text: The growbay pump seizes. {crew.botanist} drains the flooded bed, hand-waters the others, and sleeps in the growbay.
